## 2 Optimal control of second-order systems

The optimal control problem for second-order systems, under sufficient differentiability conditions can be treated exactly as in Eq. (3). There, the augmented running cost featured inside the integral was a function on T ∗ M⊕ M E . In the second-order case, this naturally leads to an augmented running cost on T ∗ T Q⊕ T Q E . Assuming adapted local coordinates ( q, v, λ q , λ v ) on T ∗ T Q , and a generic controlled SODE X = v ∂ q + f ( q, v, u ) ∂ v , Eq. (3) transforms into

- (state dynamics) ˙ q ( t ) = v ( t ), ˙ v ( t ) = f ( x ( t ) , v ( t ) , u ( t )),
- (adjoint dynamics) ˙ λ q ( t ) ⊤ = D 1 C ( q ( t ) , v ( t ) , u ( t )) -λ v ( t ) ⊤ D 1 f ( q ( t ) , v ( t ) , u ( t )), ˙ λ v ( t ) ⊤ = D 2 C ( q ( t ) , v ( t ) , u ( t )) -λ v ( t ) ⊤ D 2 f ( q ( t ) , v ( t ) , u ( t )) -λ q ( t ) ⊤ ,

while those provided by ˜ J 2 are

- (adjoint dynamics) ¨ κ ( t ) ⊤ = d dt [ D 2 C ( q ( t ) , ˙ q ( t ) , u ( t )) -κ ( t ) ⊤ D 2 f ( q ( t ) , ˙ q ( t ) , u ( t )) ] -D 1 C ( q ( t ) , ˙ q ( t ) , u ( t )) + κ ( t ) ⊤ D 1 f ( q ( t ) , ˙ q ( t ) , u ( t )),

Theorem 2.1. The necessary optimality conditions provided by ˜ J 1 and ˜ J 2 are equivalent under the identification λ v = κ .
